answer: Proof-of-stake protocols enforce Sybil resistance by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral. This creates a spiral of increasing financial risk for attackers attempting to mint multiple identities. By demanding a cryptographic cipher to prove ownership of these staked assets, the network ensures that resource scarcity prevents cheap replication. This velvet barrier to entry forces an attacker to purchase prohibitive amounts of stake, effectively making the cost of network manipulation exceed the potential gain.
